ctx.x: Boogie Woogie was popular and John had put it together the three greatest exponents of that style of piano playing. They were Meade Lux Lewis, Pete Johnson and Albert Ammons. But the Cafe only Pete Johnson and Albert Ammons were working as a team, and there was a great blues singer named "Big" Joe Turner whom the two boogie woogie pianists accompanied. And the three of them would really rock the joint every night. And they could drink plenty of booze and carry it well.

Another act was called the Golden Gate Quartet. Their names were Bill Johnson, Clyde Redick, Wilson and . They had a style of singing gospel songs which I had never heard before. In fact I didn't know anything about gospel singing except what I had heard in Baptist churches. But this was more like Holy-Holy singing to me, because it had a jazz rhythm and these fellows slap their thighs with their hands in four-four rhythm; and Yank accompanied them on drums with wire brushes on the snare drum and the joint kept…

The other act was a young woman named Hazel Scott. Hazel was a classical pianist who would play a classical number as it was supposed to be played, and then do the same number in jazz. She was well trained and was also an arranger and jazz singer. Yank also accompanied her with wire brushes. In fact he played only wire brushes which sometime didn't give the band the push it needed on certain numbers.
